summary: Richard P. Boyle studied at the University of Colorado Boulder, McGill, Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa (PhD 1982), Düsseldorf, and Washington University in St. Louis, as well as under Joshu Sasaki. He was an associate professor at Oregon Health & Science University (1986–2000).

Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Toronto (1982) under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He taught at McGill University (1988–2003) and served as associate professor at the University of New Mexico (2003–2013).
Richard Peter Hottelet was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and was attested at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1971.
Richard Phené Spiers worked in history and archaeology. He was educated at King's College London from circa 1856 to 1858 and at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts from circa 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and studied under Albrecht Weber. He served as professor at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902) and held the Lehrstuhl für Indologie at Berlin (1902–1908).

Richard Polenberg was an American history scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University (PhD circa 1959–1964). He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University (1966–2011) and was a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (circa 1970–1971).

Richard S. Cohen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, having studied under Luis Oscar Gómez and Walter M. Spink. He held a post as Associate Professor of South Asian Religious Literatures at the University of California, San Diego.

Richard Schechner studied at Cornell University, the University of Iowa, and Tulane University. Beginning circa 1967, he served as a University Professor at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts.

Richard Scherzl was a linguist who studied at Charles University, Saint Petersburg State University, and the University of Kharkiv. He directed Odesa University (1886) and held docent and professorship appointments at the University of Kharkiv between 1882 and 1894.

Indologist Richard Schmidt earned his PhD (1890) and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He was a librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1904–1910) before becoming an ordinary professor at the University of Münster (1910, 1919).
Richard Shilleto was a scholar in linguistics who was educated at Repton School, Shrewsbury School (circa 1823–1828), and Trinity College, Cambridge (circa 1828–1832).

Richard Simon was an Indologist who completed his PhD at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, also studying under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch. He later served as a privatdozent (1892) and extraordinary professor (1906) at the University of Munich.

Richard Sorabji is a scholar of philosophy and Indology educated at Pembroke College, Oxford. He served on the faculty at Cornell University (circa 1962–1970), as professor of philosophy at King's College London (circa 1970–2000), and at Gresham College (circa 2000–2006).

Richard Sproat is a computational linguist who studied at UC San Diego and MIT (PhD 1985). He held posts at Bell Labs (1985–1999), University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2003–2009), Oregon Health & Science University (2009–2012), Google (2012, 2019), and Sakana AI (2024).
Richard Stothert was an Indologist who completed his studies at the University of Glasgow and the University of Edinburgh. He served as the Principal of Wilson College in Mumbai from 1876 to 1884.

Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (circa 1953–1957) and Princeton University (circa 1958–1963). He held appointments at the University of Sydney (circa 1963–1964) and as a fellow at the Australian National University (1971).

Richard Taupier works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MS and doctorate at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he became Associate Director of Research Development, and was a visiting lecturer at Smith College.

Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who earned his Sanskrit doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He served as dean at UT Austin (1999–2006), provost at Kansas (2006–2009), president of Oregon (2009–2011), and president of the Field Museum (2012–2020).

Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tübingen from circa 1891 to 1895. He was a guest professor at Peking University (1923) and held the Lehrstuhl für Sinologie at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1924, which he founded in 1925.

Richard von Garbe was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen (PhD 1877). He taught at the University of Königsberg (1878–1895) and served as chair holder at the University of Tübingen from 1895 to 1927.
